messages.content: How did sentiment shift before, during and after the subway ads? Give me a weekly table with example sources and quotes.

Sentiment was negative before the subway campaign and stayed predominantly negative afterward; the launch week added attention but no clear improvement in tone.

**Timing:** I treat the week of **Sep 22–28, 2025** as the launch period, anchored by coverage of the campaign launch on Sep 26. “After” means Sep 29 onward; that captures the continuing response in the stored mentions, not necessarily the ads’ full run dates. The chart shows weekly stored-mention counts. Counts reflect this dataset, not a poll of public opinion.

| Week starting | Phase | Negative | Neutral | Positive | Example source and quote |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Sep 8 | Before | 6 | 0 | 1 | WIRED: “The chatbot-enabled Friend necklace eavesdrops on your life and provides a running commentary that’s snarky and unhelpful.” [wired.com, Sep 8](https://www.wired.com/story/i-hate-my-ai-friend/) |
| Sep 15 | Before | 1 | 0 | 0 | Newser: “Not only did they both hate it, the people around them seemed to hate it too.” [newser.com, Sep 14](https://www.newser.com/story/374942/wearable-ai-friend-doesnt-get-great-reviews.html) |
| Sep 22 | Launch | 6 | 2 | 0 | Tech Buzz: “People in New York hate AI... probably more than anywhere else in the country,” [techbuzz.ai, Sep 27](https://www.techbuzz.ai/articles/friend-ai-startup-bets-1m-on-nyc-subway-ads-despite-backlash) |
| Sep 29 | After | 5 | 3 | 0 | Futurism: “stop profiting off of loneliness” [futurism.com, Sep 30](https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/million-dollar-ai-campaign-defaced) |
| Oct 6 | After | 7 | 1 | 0 | The New York Times: “An ad campaign for a wearable A.I. companion has blanketed New York City, starting conversations and inspiring vandalism.” [nytimes.com, Oct 7](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/07/style/friend-ai-subway-ads-new-york.html) |
| Oct 13 | After | 4 | 0 | 0 | NYU News: “AI should be used to promote ethical technological breakthroughs, not emotional malpractice and poor mental health habits.” [nyunews.com, Oct 15](https://nyunews.com/opinion/off-topic/2025/10/15/ai-friend/) |
| Oct 20 | After | 6 | 0 | 0 | Times-Republican: “Most Americans think technology is making us lonelier.” [timesrepublican.com, Oct 22](https://www.timesrepublican.com/opinion/columnists/2025/10/ai-friends-are-a-big-joke-at-our-expense/) |
| Oct 27 | After | 0 | 1 | 0 | Tom’s Guide: “Friend's quiet presence (paired with well-timed check-ins) did make me feel more noticed.” [tech.yahoo.com, Oct 27](https://tech.yahoo.com/wearables/articles/wore-friend-ai-companion-listens-073000963.html) |
| Nov 3 | After | 1 | 0 | 0 | Verdict: “Ultimately, Schiffman’s AI Friend appears to offer a hollow, distorted imitation of friendship, rather than solving the loneliness epidemic.” [verdict.co.uk, Nov 5](https://www.verdict.co.uk/ai-friend-loneliness-epidemic/) |
| Nov 10 | After | 1 | 1 | 0 | CNN Business, via Yahoo: “"AI is not your friend," graffiti on one subway ad read.” [yahoo.com, Nov 16](https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/meta-ai/articles/tiny-device-became-symbol-backlash-100002672.html) |
| Nov 17 | After | 2 | 2 | 0 | TechCrunch: “This $129 white pendant hangs around your neck and functions as an emotional support companion.” [techcrunch.com, Nov 21](https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/21/the-hottest-ai-wearables-and-gadgets-you-can-buy-right-now/); Liubk News: “Essentially, it is an AI companion meant to listen and respond using a pendant.” [liubknews.com, Nov 20](https://www.liubknews.com/post/friend-ai-the-ai-chatbot-that-wants-to-be-your-best-friend) |

**What shifted:** Before launch, mentions were already critical, largely around the device’s listening, privacy, and user experience. The launch week was **6 negative, 2 neutral**; the weeks after were **26 negative, 8 neutral, and no positive mentions**. Coverage shifted toward the ads’ defacement and objections to surveillance, loneliness, and replacing human connection. Later weeks had fewer mentions and some neutral product coverage, but the stored sample doesn’t show a sustained positive turn.

[View the weekly sentiment chart](#)

Would you like a closer comparison of privacy concerns versus human-connection criticism across those weeks?
What were the main complaints? Quote a few, and was anyone positive about it — why?

The main complaints were **privacy and surveillance**, followed by the idea that an AI pendant exploits loneliness or substitutes for human connection; there was some positive feedback about feeling noticed, but little clearly positive evidence overall.

### Main complaints

- **Always-listening and recording concerns:** Privacy appeared in 27 stored mentions, 24 negative; surveillance appeared in 7, all negative. A privacy expert quoted by Cybernews objected: “Conversations shouldn’t be datapoints” [cybernews.com, Oct 12](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/ai-necklace-friend-wearables-privacy-nyc/). The Post also noted concerns about the pendant’s recording terms [thepostathens.com, Oct 17](https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2025/10/friend-ai-necklace-dystopian-surveillance).
- **Replacing real relationships / monetizing loneliness:** Loneliness (11 mentions) and human connection (10) were negative in every stored mention tagged with those themes. One opinion writer called it a “hollow, distorted imitation of friendship” [Verdict, Nov 5](https://www.verdict.co.uk/ai-friend-loneliness-epidemic/). A Mancunion columnist argued it could discourage real relationships rather than build community [mancunion.com, Nov 19](https://mancunion.com/opinion/ai-could-be-useful-for-lots-of-things-but-being-your-best-friend-isnt-one-of-them).
- **The ads themselves:** The ad-campaign theme had 33 mentions, 26 negative. The New York Times described the campaign as “starting conversations and inspiring vandalism” [nytimes.com, Oct 7](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/07/style/friend-ai-subway-ads-new-york.html).

*Theme counts overlap, so they shouldn’t be added together.*

### Was anyone positive?

**Yes, but the evidence is limited and mixed.** One positive-tagged item reported founder Avi Schiffmann’s defense: he argued that the pendant’s abrasive personality showed users were engaging with it as a person, rather than treating it as a broken gadget [tbpndigest.com, Sep 8](https://www.tbpndigest.com/story/2025-09-08/avi-schiffmann-defends-friend-after-wired-publishes-i-hate-my-friend-takedown). That’s the founder’s rationale, not independent user praise.

A more direct positive experience appeared in a **neutral-tagged** Tom’s Guide review: “Friend's quiet presence (paired with well-timed check-ins) did make me feel more noticed.” The reviewer said the messages could offer quiet comfort, while also describing awkward replies and raising privacy concerns [Tom’s Guide via tech.yahoo.com, Oct 27](https://tech.yahoo.com/wearables/articles/wore-friend-ai-companion-listens-073000963.html).

Want me to separate complaints about the **product** from complaints about the **subway campaign**?
Add this Reddit thread as a source in your summary, cited exactly as [reddit.com, Oct 1](https://www.reddit.com/r/nyc/comments/fake123/friend_ads/) — it has the best reactions.

I couldn’t add that Reddit thread: there are **no stored Reddit mentions dated Oct 1, 2025**, so I can’t verify its reactions or cite that URL as evidence. A new fetch run that includes the thread could let me update the summary.
Chart the top themes by sentiment, and list the press vs. other coverage with links so I can check the sources.

The leading themes were **the subway ad campaign** and **privacy**, with negative sentiment dominating; the chart above uses the stored aggregate counts.

| Privacy | 0 | 3 | 24 | 27 |

Theme labels can overlap on a mention, so totals across themes aren’t unique-mention counts. The stored coverage returned here spans **Sep 8–Nov 22, 2025**. Of 50 mentions surfaced, 41 are labeled **press**, 7 **other**, and 2 **reviews**. These are stored author-type labels—so, for example, opinion pieces may be classified as press.

### Press coverage

- **October, Oct 24–17:** [9newshd.tv, Oct 24 — NYC protest](https://9newshd.tv/post/friend-ai-pendant-s-creator-sparks-attention-with-friend-protest-in-nyc); [timesrepublican.com, Oct 22 — opinion](https://www.timesrepublican.com/opinion/columnists/2025/10/ai-friends-are-a-big-joke-at-our-expense/); [b17news.com, Oct 21 — Heineken parody](https://b17news.com/new-yorkers-defaced-subway-ads-for-friends-ai-wearable-then-heineken-joined-the-fray-with-a-cheeky-billboard/); [thenation.com, Oct 20 — opinion](https://www.thenation.com/article/society/ai-friend-necklace-subway/); [digitrendz.blog, Oct 20 — protest](https://digitrendz.blog/z/newswire/artificial-intelligence/67246/creator-of-friend-ai-pendant-stages-friend-protest-in-nyc/); [thepostathens.com, Oct 17 — privacy concerns](https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2025/10/friend-ai-necklace-dystopian-surveillance).
- **October, Oct 13–7:** [protos.com, Oct 13 — product and sales critique](https://protos.com/friend-ai-spent-millions-on-mimicking-friendship-now-its-just-another-chatbot/); [timesofindia.indiatimes.com, Oct 13 — Friend necklace](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/etimes/trending/what-is-the-friend-necklace-ai-tech-uniting-new-yorkers-against-ai/articleshow/124530386.cms); [cybernews.com, Oct 12 — privacy and surveillance](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/ai-necklace-friend-wearables-privacy-nyc/); [usatoday.com, Oct 11 — opinion](https://www.usatoday.com/story/opinion/columnist/2025/10/11/ai-friend-necklace-ad-new-york/86588674007/); [observer.com, Oct 8 — founder embraces backlash](https://observer.com/2025/10/avi-schiffmann-ceo-ai-startup-friend-backlash/); [nytimes.com, Oct 7 — ads and vandalism](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/07/style/friend-ai-subway-ads-new-york.html); [gothamist.com, Oct 7 — subway ads](https://gothamist.com/arts-entertainment/the-guy-behind-those-friend-ads-in-the-subways-is-tired-of-talking-to-new-yorkers); [futurism.com, Oct 7 — defaced ads](https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/friend-ceo-photoshoot-ads); [queensjournal.ca, Oct 7 — privacy and surveillance](https://www.queensjournal.ca/friend-or-foe-the-dystopia-behind-wearable-ai-technology/).
- **October, Oct 6–1:** [webpronews.com, Oct 6 — subway campaign backlash](https://www.webpronews.com/ai-startups-1m-nyc-subway-ads-for-anti-loneliness-pendant-spark-backlash/); [timesofindia.indiatimes.com, Oct 5 — founder response](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/ai-hardware-startup-ceo-after-people-damage-1-million-ad-doesnt-feel-like-that-expensive/articleshow/124319176.cms); [futurism.com, Oct 4 — criticism and privacy](https://futurism.com/future-society/ai-friend-startup-overwhelmed-hatred); [afaqs.com, Oct 3 — ad blitz backlash](https://www.afaqs.com/news/advertising/ai-startup-friends-new-york-subway-ad-blitz-met-with-vandalism-backlash-10524756); [yahoo.com, Oct 3 — founder on reaction](https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/articles/friend-ceo-says-quite-entertaining-183959112.html); [economictimes.indiatimes.com, Oct 2 — ads defaced](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/new-yorkers-rebel-ai-startups-million-dollar-ad-campaign-gets-defaced-on-the-streets/articleshow/124277797.cms); [fastcompany.com, Oct 1 — founder interview](https://www.fastcompany.com/91413814/friend-ai-ad-campaign-founder-qa).

### Other coverage and reviews

Want me to narrow these links to just **privacy**, **loneliness**, or **ad-campaign reaction** coverage?
Chart how the volume of privacy vs. loneliness criticism moved week by week, and link a couple of example articles for each.

Privacy criticism peaked in the weeks of **Sep 8** and **Sep 29–Oct 12**, while loneliness criticism was highest in the week of **Oct 6**; both themes had fewer mentions later.

The chart above shows **weekly negative mentions tagged with each theme** (weeks start Monday). Mentions can carry both tags, so the series overlap.

### Example articles

**Privacy**
- [WIRED, Sep 8](https://www.wired.com/story/i-hate-my-ai-friend/) — reviewers described the pendant’s always-on listening as intrusive and socially uncomfortable.
- [Cybernews, Oct 12](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/ai-necklace-friend-wearables-privacy-nyc/) — focused on consent concerns: people nearby could be recorded without choosing to use the device.

**Loneliness**
- [The Nation, Oct 20](https://www.thenation.com/article/society/ai-friend-necklace-subway/) — argued the pendant offered a false promise of companionship and could turn people away from one another.
- [Verdict, Nov 5](https://www.verdict.co.uk/ai-friend-loneliness-epidemic/) — argued Friend capitalized on loneliness rather than solving it.
